## Shaghalny (شغلني)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/shaghalny/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/shaghalny/
Sector: Services
Founders: Omar Khalifa
Outcome: deal
Shaghalny pitched in Season 2, episode 2. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas: 5M EGP for 35%.
عرض فريق شغلني مشروعه في الموسم ٢، الحلقة ٢. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أيمن عباس بقيمة ٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٣٥٪؜.
Shaghalny, whose name means "hire me", is an online jobs platform for blue- and grey-collar workers and candidates with intermediate qualifications. Founder Omar Khalifa came up with it at university, and it took seed funding from Naguib Sawiris's Gemini Holding in 2016; it has since built a database of more than 1.7 million jobseekers and thousands of hiring companies. On Shark Tank he closed a deal for EGP 5 million in exchange for 35%, and the company later opened physical hiring centres, starting in Sohag and then Greater Cairo, where jobseekers are interviewed on the spot. The show lists it among Ayman Abbas's first three investments on Shark Tank Egypt.

## Not Foods (نوت فودز)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/not-foods/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/not-foods/
Sector: Food
Founders: Amir Abboud, Germine Abboud

Not Foods pitched in Season 2, episode 2. The founders asked for 4M EGP for 30%, valuing the company at 13.3M EGP. They left without a deal.

NOT Foods is an Egyptian brand of 100% plant-based food, often described as a pioneer of vegan eating in Egypt. Its range of meat-free alternatives includes burgers, "chicken" nuggets and a vegan mozzarella that melts like the real thing, letting people swap junk-food favourites for healthier versions. Its products are sold in Cairo supermarkets such as The Grocer, Sunny Market and Mahmoud Elfar. The brand was founded by Amir and Germine Abboud.

## Supply List (سبلاي ليست)

Supply List is an Egyptian retail startup that takes the stress out of back-to-school shopping. Each year parents receive long lists of required school supplies and have to hunt for every item themselves. Supply List lets them order the whole list in about 20 seconds through its website, thesupplylist.co. The company won a deal on Shark Tank Egypt, where Mohamed Farouk invested EGP 4 million for a 51% stake.

Blooms Egypt is a performing-arts and youth-education company that has spent 13 years developing children's personality, culture and skills. ## Sympl (سيمبل)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/simple/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/simple/
Sector: Fintech
Founders: Mohamed El-Feky, Yasmine Henna, Karim Tawfik
Outcome: no deal

Sympl is an Egyptian payment platform that lets shoppers split purchases into short-term, interest-free payments at participating stores and websites. Customers choose a payment plan, pay a one-time service fee and track their payment dates in the app. Its official FAQ states that the bank-card balance must cover the full purchase amount at checkout. The platform also partners with retailers to offer instalments to their customers.

## LabTronic (لابترونيك)

LabTronic is an Egyptian manufacturer that designs and builds educational lab equipment for engineering faculties and technical schools. ## Schoolz (سكولز)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/schoolz/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/schoolz/
Sector: Services
Founders: Hosny Ahmed, Abdel Monsef Ismail, Ayman Hamza
Outcome: unconfirmed
Schoolz pitched in Season 1, episode 11. The founders asked for 15M EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 150M EGP. No public source confirms the outcome yet.
عرض فريق سكولز مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١١. طلب المؤسسون ١٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٥٠ مليون ج.م. لا يوجد مصدر علني يؤكد نتيجة العرض حتى الآن.
Schoolz is a Cairo-based platform for safe, affordable student transport to school. It uses qualified drivers, a supervisor in every vehicle, live cameras that let parents watch their children, and notifications from pick-up to drop-off. Founded in 2020 as a pandemic-era experiment, it was soon asked to serve schools, sports academies and clubs. It raised a six-figure pre-seed round from Saudi and Egyptian investors in 2021, and a six-figure investment from EdVentures in 2025.

## Asfoura (عصفورة)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/asfoura/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/asfoura/
Sector: Education
Founders: Maram Khamis
Outcome: deal
Asfoura pitched in Season 1, episode 11. The founders asked for 2.5M EGP for 20%, valuing the company at 12.5M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Abdallah Sallam, Ahmed El Sewedy and Mohamed Farouk: 2.5M EGP for 30%.
عرض فريق عصفورة مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١١. طلب المؤسسون ٢٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٢٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٢٫٥ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع عبد الله سلام، أحمد السويدي ومحمد فاروق بقيمة ٢٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٣٠٪؜.
Asfoura is the first Egyptian publisher dedicated to children's books and stories written in Egyptian colloquial Arabic, founded in Cairo in 2021 to help children build their spoken Arabic in a familiar, unintimidating way. Many of its titles revolve around Egyptian food, such as Waraa Shagar, about two friends cooking molokhia, and Kahk El-Eid, about a boy baking kahk with his grandmother, and it pairs the books with hands-on cooking workshops. It sold about 3,200 books in its latest year. The sharks competed fiercely to win over founder Maram Khamis, and she accepted a joint offer of EGP 2.5 million for 30% from Abdallah Sallam, Ahmed El Sewedy and Mohamed Farouk.

## Chef's House (شيفس هاوس)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/chefs-house/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/chefs-house/
Sector: Food
Founders: Mostafa Wahdan
Outcome: unconfirmed
Chef's House pitched in Season 1, episode 10. The founders asked for 10M EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 100M EGP. No public source confirms the outcome yet.
عرض فريق شيفس هاوس مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١٠. طلب المؤسسون ١٠ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٠٠ مليون ج.م. لا يوجد مصدر علني يؤكد نتيجة العرض حتى الآن.
Chef's House is a cloud kitchen in Nasr City, Cairo, founded in 2021. It runs on a kitchen-as-a-service (KaaS) model: it prepares, cooks, packages and delivers food for several restaurant brands from one shared kitchen, and it also runs its own virtual restaurants. Partner brands get operational reporting and data analysis along with the cooking, which helps them grow without opening new branches. Co-founder Mostafa Wahdan says he started the company to help restaurants keep operating and widen their delivery reach.

## Can Bank (كان بنك)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/can-bank/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/can-bank/
Sector: Other
Founders: Islam El Refaey
Outcome: no deal
Can Bank pitched in Season 1, episode 10. The founders asked for 1.5M EGP for 5%, valuing the company at 30M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق كان بنك مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١٠. طلب المؤسسون ١٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٣٠ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
CanBank is a smart reverse vending machine built by the Egyptian startup ZeroPrime Technologies. People drop in empty plastic bottles and aluminium cans, and the machine identifies and sorts them, then rewards the user with mobile credit, discounts on services or a donation to charity. Its machines are installed at universities and public spaces around Cairo, including the New Administrative Capital, and supermarkets are next. The business now funds itself and aims to have 20,000 machines across Egypt by 2030.

## Tomatiki (توماتيكي)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/tomatiki/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/tomatiki/
Sector: Agriculture
Founders: Mohamed Barakat
Outcome: deal
Tomatiki pitched in Season 1, episode 10. The founders asked for 2M EGP for 5%, valuing the company at 40M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ahmed El Sewedy: 2M EGP for 50%.
عرض فريق توماتيكي مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١٠. طلب المؤسسون ٢ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٤٠ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أحمد السويدي بقيمة ٢ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٠٪؜.
Tomatiki makes smart irrigation and greenhouse devices that cut fertilizer and energy use, sold with a 10-year warranty that surprised the sharks. Based in Heliopolis, Cairo, it designs its systems in-house, from hardware and firmware to a cloud platform for remote monitoring and control, and also covers fertigation, aquaculture and green-space management. Mohamed Farouk challenged founder Mohamed Barakat on offering such a warranty as a young company, and the pitch ended in a deal with Ahmed El Sewedy for EGP 2 million.

## Portal (بورتال)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/portal/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/portal/
Sector: Tech
Founders: Ahmed Mahfouz
Outcome: deal
Portal pitched in Season 1, episode 10. The founders asked for 10K EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 100K EGP. They walked away with a deal: 10K EGP.
عرض فريق بورتال مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١٠. طلب المؤسسون ١٠ ألف ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٠٠ ألف ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة بقيمة ١٠ ألف ج.م.
Portal is an Egyptian tech startup founded by Ahmed Mahfouz that builds affordable versions of eye-catching technology, such as hologram shows and an advertising robot. Holographic displays and promotional robots usually cost a lot, which puts them out of reach for most local brands, events and venues. Portal's aim is to make these attention-grabbing experiences cheap enough for smaller businesses to use. Ahmed Mahfouz brought the idea to Shark Tank Egypt in Season 1.

## Peacock Designs (بيكوك ديزاينز)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/peacock-designs/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/peacock-designs/
Sector: Home
Founders: Dalia Salem, Mostafa El-Sayed
Outcome: unconfirmed
Peacock Designs pitched in Season 1, episode 9. The founders asked for 10M EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 100M EGP. No public source confirms the outcome yet.
عرض فريق بيكوك ديزاينز مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٩. طلب المؤسسون ١٠ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٠٠ مليون ج.م. لا يوجد مصدر علني يؤكد نتيجة العرض حتى الآن.
Peacock Designs, founded by Dalia Salem and Mostafa El-Sayed, upcycles palm fronds and leaves into furniture and home products instead of letting them be burned after each harvest. The idea grew from Salem's move to Tunis village in Fayoum, where she began making beds, wardrobes and a library for her own home from palm material. The EU-funded online store works with local artisans and designers, and the company has spent EGP 2 million on research and development to make the process more efficient. The founders asked the sharks for EGP 10 million for 10%, valuing the company at EGP 100 million.

## Career 180 (كارير 180)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/career-180/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/career-180/
Sector: Services
Founders: Mohamed Akmal, Shorouk Alaa
Outcome: no deal
Career 180 pitched in Season 1, episode 9. The founders asked for 3M EGP for 5%, valuing the company at 60M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق كارير 180 مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٩. طلب المؤسسون ٣ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٦٠ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
Career 180 is a career-development and hiring platform that prepares young Arab talent for the job market, combining online mentoring and career advice with offline events such as the Egypt Career Summit. It lists more than 1,500 jobs and has around 250,000 users. Backed by EdVentures, which invested in 2019 and 2021, it raised further funding in 2025 from Den VC to expand into Saudi Arabia, Oman and Malta. On the show, founders Mohamed Akmal and Shorouk Alaa asked for EGP 3 million for 5%; the sharks countered with EGP 7 million for 30%, and the founders turned it down.

## Kids Kit (كيدز كيت)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/kids-kit/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/kids-kit/
Sector: Services
Founders: Mariam El Shabakshy
Outcome: deal
Kids Kit pitched in Season 1, episode 9. The founders asked for 5M EGP for 15%, valuing the company at 33.3M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas: 5M EGP for 40%.

Kids Kit (Kidzkit) is billed as the first online marketplace in Egypt and the MENA region for renting baby and children's gear, letting families rent used items for less instead of buying them new. It also helps mothers earn a side income by renting out the gear their own children have outgrown. Founder Mariam El Shabakshy charmed the sharks from her opening and asked for EGP 5 million for 15%, leaving with a deal. ## Skoolix (سكوليكس)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/skoolix/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/skoolix/
Sector: Education
Founders: Fady Osama
Outcome: no deal
Skoolix pitched in Season 1, episode 9. The founders asked for 7M EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 70M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق سكوليكس مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٩. طلب المؤسسون ٧ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ٧٠ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
Skoolix is an Alexandria-based school platform, founded in 2020, that brings students, parents, teachers and school administration together in one app. Schools use it for real-time updates, assignments, attendance, grades and reports and online fee payments, through iOS, Android and Huawei apps plus a web admin panel. Founder Fady Osama asked for EGP 7 million for 10%; the sharks liked the idea but balked at the high valuation, and Abdallah Sallam questioned why the profitable company needed investors.

## Sporty Pro (سبورتي برو)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/sporty-pro/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/sporty-pro/
Sector: Retail
Founders: Sherif Zahran, Tamiran Shalaby
Outcome: deal
Sporty Pro pitched in Season 1, episode 8. The founders asked for 3.5M EGP for 7.5%, valuing the company at 46.7M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ahmed El Sewedy and Mohamed Farouk: 3.5M EGP for 40%.
عرض فريق سبورتي برو مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٨. طلب المؤسسون ٣٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٧٫٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٤٦٫٧ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أحمد السويدي ومحمد فاروق بقيمة ٣٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٤٠٪؜.
Sporty Pro is an AI-driven online store and app for sportswear, sports shoes and athleisure, based in Sheikh Zayed City. It carries more than 30 brands, from Adidas, Nike, Puma and Reebok to Egyptian labels such as Magma, Sigma Fit, Fit Freak and Atum. Launched in April 2022 with iOS and Android apps following later that year, it had served over 19,000 customers and planned to expand into Saudi Arabia. Founders Sherif Zahran and Tamer Shalaby asked for EGP 3.5 million for 7.5% and closed a deal with Ahmed El Sewedy and Mohamed Farouk.

## Efika (إفيكا)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/evica/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/evica/
Sector: Tech
Founders: Mohamed Mahmoud
Outcome: no deal
Efika pitched in Season 1, episode 8. The founders asked for 4.5M EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 45M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق إفيكا مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٨. طلب المؤسسون ٤٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ٤٥ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
Efika is an Egyptian manufacturer of robots that clean solar panels. Dust and dirt can cut a panel's output sharply, and cleaning by hand is slow, uses a lot of water and can be unsafe. Efika's automatic and semi-automatic robots clean panels in dry or wet mode for mid- to large-scale solar plants and solar street-light poles. The company says this restores up to 25% of the power lost to soiling. Founded in 2021 in Giza, it has raised about $250K in angel funding.

## Cosmos Bionics (كوزموس بايونيكس)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/cosmos-bionics/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/cosmos-bionics/
Sector: Health
Founders: Mina Ashraf, Gihan Abdallah
Outcome: deal
Cosmos Bionics pitched in Season 1, episode 8. The founders asked for 3M EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 30M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas: 3M EGP for 10%.
عرض فريق كوزموس بايونيكس مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٨. طلب المؤسسون ٣ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ٣٠ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أيمن عباس بقيمة ٣ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜.
Cosmos Bionics is an Alexandria startup, founded in 2022, that builds a lightweight powered exoskeleton to help people who have lost mobility stand and walk. The Cosmos is a lower-body hip-and-knee suit driven by motors in the joints and steered by the user shifting their posture; the company says it is the first powered exoskeleton developed in Egypt. It addresses a need it puts at over 2 million Egyptians and 500 million people worldwide. CEO Mina Ashraf's pitch moved the sharks, and the founders closed a deal with Ayman Abbas for EGP 3 million for 10%, earmarked for research and ISO 13485 and CE certification.

Calmy is an Egyptian brand that makes ergonomic baby carriers, designed so mothers can carry their little ones comfortably while keeping babies safely supported. It answers a common problem for new parents: carriers that strain the back and shoulders or hold the baby in an awkward position. Calmy sells its carriers online, and by the time it pitched on Shark Tank Egypt it had already sold more than 4,000 units.

Jojo's Ranch is a cattle ranch that raises its own animals and sells all kinds of meat and prime cuts at imported quality but lower prices. ## Choroida (كورويدا)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/choroida/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/choroida/
Sector: Health
Founders: Sameh Nabil
Outcome: unconfirmed
Choroida pitched in Season 1, episode 6. The founders asked for 8M EGP for 5%, valuing the company at 160M EGP. No public source confirms the outcome yet.
عرض فريق كورويدا مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٦. طلب المؤسسون ٨ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٦٠ مليون ج.م. لا يوجد مصدر علني يؤكد نتيجة العرض حتى الآن.
Choroida is an Egyptian health-tech venture building a medical device for examining and imaging the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye. Retinal checks are central to catching eye disease early, and Choroida's goal is a device that lets clinicians both inspect and capture images of the retina. Founder Sameh Nabil brought the project to Season 1 of Shark Tank Egypt, where his pitch became one of the episode's most talked-about moments.

## Bikado (بيكادو)

Bikado is an Egyptian language-practice app for children that teaches through hands-on practice rather than rote memorisation, drawing on a European teaching method. ## Mandoobak Smart (مندوبك سمارت)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/mandoobak-smart/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/mandoobak-smart/
Sector: Tech
Founders: Mostafa Wasfy, Mohamed El Hafez
Outcome: deal
Mandoobak Smart pitched in Season 1, episode 5. The founders asked for 7M EGP for 15%, valuing the company at 46.7M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Mohamed Farouk and Ahmed El Sewedy: 7M EGP for 35%.
عرض فريق مندوبك سمارت مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٥. طلب المؤسسون ٧ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٤٦٫٧ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع محمد فاروق وأحمد السويدي بقيمة ٧ مليون ج.م مقابل ٣٥٪؜.
Mandoobak Smart is an app that lets grocers and supermarket owners order everything their shops need from one page, at company prices and with free delivery, saving them time and effort. It started in Aswan in January 2022 and drew on its founders' 12 years of experience selling food to grocery stores; by the pitch it had reached EGP 7 million in sales. The founders also described a smart shelf that detects low stock and reorders through the app. They asked for EGP 7 million for 15%, were the first to haggle with Mohamed Farouk until he told them “take it or leave it”, and closed at EGP 7 million for 35% with Mohamed Farouk and Ahmed El Sewedy.

## Tutoruu (توتورو)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/tutoro/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/tutoro/
Sector: Education
Founders: Seif Amr Kassem, Mariam Amer, Youssef Abdelhamid, Mohamed Samer
Outcome: unconfirmed
Tutoruu pitched in Season 1, episode 5. The founders asked for 4M EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 40M EGP. No public source confirms the outcome yet.
عرض فريق توتورو مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٥. طلب المؤسسون ٤ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ٤٠ مليون ج.م. لا يوجد مصدر علني يؤكد نتيجة العرض حتى الآن.
Tutoruu is a university tutoring platform that connects students with peers who have already completed their courses. It offers one-to-one tutoring, study groups, expert questions and answers, and Ruu AI learning tools. Seif Amr Kassem, Mariam Amer and Mohamed Samer presented the business on Shark Tank Egypt, asking for EGP 4 million for 10%. Forbes also identifies Youssef Abdelhamid as a co-founder.

## Plus Gear (بلس جير)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/plus-gear/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/plus-gear/
Sector: Sports
Founders: Kamal Abu El Kheir
Outcome: no deal
Plus Gear pitched in Season 1, episode 5. The founders asked for 1.2M EGP for 15%, valuing the company at 8M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق بلس جير مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٥. طلب المؤسسون ١٫٢ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٨ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
Plus Gear is an Egyptian sports startup behind a wearable fitness vest that you put on while you train. It is built for people who want to exercise at home without a gym, and for athletes who want their daily training to be simpler. The vest goes on over your workout clothes and fits into your normal exercise routine. Founder Kamal Abu El Kheir brought the product to Season 1 of Shark Tank Egypt to raise money to grow the brand.

## Tap Tag (تاب تاج)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/tap-tag/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/tap-tag/
Sector: Tech
Founders: Youssef Samir
Outcome: deal
Tap Tag pitched in Season 1, episode 5. The founders asked for 370K EGP for 15%, valuing the company at 2.5M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas and Abdallah Sallam: 370K EGP for 15%.
عرض فريق تاب تاج مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٥. طلب المؤسسون ٣٧٠ ألف ج.م مقابل ١٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٢٫٥ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أيمن عباس وعبد الله سلام بقيمة ٣٧٠ ألف ج.م مقابل ١٥٪؜.
Tap Tag is an app that lets shoppers scan a clothing item with their phone to see where it is sold, its size and its quality, along with the nearest store. A tag on the garment is read by the device and is designed to come off only after several washes. Its founder, Youssef Samir, was 14 and billed as the youngest entrepreneur on the show when the episode aired on CBC in February 2023. He asked for EGP 370,000 for 15% and got that deal from Ayman Abbas and Abdallah Sallam.

## Agrcology (أجركولوجي)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/agrcology/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/agrcology/
Sector: Agriculture
Founders: Hisham El Banna
Outcome: deal
Agrcology pitched in Season 1, episode 4. The founders asked for 5M EGP for 25%, valuing the company at 20M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Mohamed Farouk: 5M EGP for 50%.
عرض فريق أجركولوجي مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٤. طلب المؤسسون ٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٢٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٢٠ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع محمد فاروق بقيمة ٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٠٪؜.
Agrcology is an Egyptian agritech startup that builds a smart collar for dairy cows. The collar remotely tracks each cow's movement, body temperature and overall health, so farmers can catch problems early and protect their milk output instead of relying on manual checks. Founder Hisham El Banna brought the idea to Shark Tank Egypt in Season 1, where he closed a deal with investor Mohamed Farouk.

## Virclo (فيركلو)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/fairclo/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/fairclo/
Sector: Retail
Founders: Mohamed El Kholy
Outcome: deal
Virclo pitched in Season 1, episode 4. The founders asked for 2M EGP for 5%, valuing the company at 40M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas and Ahmed El Sewedy: 2M EGP for 30%.
عرض فريق فيركلو مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٤. طلب المؤسسون ٢ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٤٠ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أيمن عباس وأحمد السويدي بقيمة ٢ مليون ج.م مقابل ٣٠٪؜.
Virclo is an Egyptian online marketplace built around a simple idea: the things you no longer need still have value to someone else. Users can list any unwanted product and choose to sell it, buy from others, or swap it for something they actually want, keeping usable items in circulation instead of in storage. Founded by Mohamed El Kholy, Virclo pitched in Season 1 of Shark Tank Egypt and closed a deal with Ayman Abbas and Ahmed El Sewedy.

## Scooby (سكوبي)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/scoopy-scooters/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/scoopy-scooters/
Sector: Tech
Founders: Bemen Wagdy
Outcome: no deal
Scooby pitched in Season 1, episode 4. The founders asked for 2.5M EGP for 5%, valuing the company at 50M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق سكوبي مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٤. طلب المؤسسون ٢٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ٥٠ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
Scooby is an Egyptian micromobility startup offering electric scooters that can be controlled remotely, giving city dwellers a quick, easy way to cover short urban trips. Riders pick up a scooter from the nearest location and ride it to where they need to go, rather than relying on cars or crowded transport for short hops. Founded by Bemen Wagdy, the company brought its concept to Shark Tank Egypt in Season 1, where a shark test-rode a scooter in the tank.

## Grif (جريف)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/grif/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/grif/
Sector: Home
Founders: Youssef El Rayan
Outcome: deal
Grif pitched in Season 1, episode 3. The founders asked for 900K EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 9M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas: 900K EGP for 10%.

Grif is an Egyptian cast-iron cookware brand that makes its pans and Dutch ovens locally, offering durable pieces at lower prices that are designed to last a lifetime. Its founders started it after struggling to find affordable cast-iron skillets in Egypt, and its Dutch ovens feature enamelled lids with brass knobs. Founder Youssef El Rayan asked for EGP 900,000 for 10% and, after weighing bigger offers from Mohamed Mansour and Abdallah Sallam, accepted Ayman Abbas's offer on exactly those terms.

## Tilestic (تايلستك)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/tilestic/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/tilestic/
Sector: Manufacturing
Founders: Mohamed Abu Kelila
Outcome: deal
Tilestic pitched in Season 1, episode 3. The founders asked for 600K EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 6M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Mohamed Ismail Mansour: 600K EGP for 10%.
عرض فريق تايلستك مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٣. طلب المؤسسون ٦٠٠ ألف ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ٦ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع محمد إسماعيل منصور بقيمة ٦٠٠ ألف ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜.
Tilestic is an Alexandria startup, founded in 2020, that turns single-use plastic waste nobody else recycles into building materials. Its own process and compound produce interlock and paver tiles for sidewalks, as well as roof tiles, made entirely from recycled plastic. The company is listed among the Solar Impulse Foundation's member companies. Founder Mohamed Abu Kelila asked for EGP 600,000 for 10% and secured that deal from Mohamed Mansour.

## Masroofi (مصروفي)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/masroufi/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/masroufi/
Sector: Fintech
Founders: Mostafa Abdel-Khabeer, Sayed Hosni
Outcome: no deal
Masroofi pitched in Season 1, episode 3. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق مصروفي مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٣. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
Masroofi ("my pocket money") is an Egyptian fintech that gives children a prepaid card and a money-learning app, so kids aged roughly 6 to 15 can spend, save and pay electronically while their parents stay in control. Parents set up a profile, top up the wallet from their own bank card and order an NFC card for their child (priced at EGP 75 in January 2023 coverage). Launched in January 2022 as Egypt's first e-wallet built for children, it issues its cards with Arab Bank and Visa and raised a $1.5 million seed round in 2023.

## MaWard (ماورد)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/mawared/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/mawared/
Sector: Beauty
Founders: Hossam El Maraghy
Outcome: deal
MaWard pitched in Season 1, episode 2. The founders asked for 2.5M EGP for 15%, valuing the company at 16.7M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas: 2.5M EGP for 51%.
عرض فريق ماورد مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٢. طلب المؤسسون ٢٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٦٫٧ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أيمن عباس بقيمة ٢٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥١٪؜.
MaWard is an Egyptian beauty brand that sells weekly skincare kits, giving customers a simple, ready-made routine instead of a shelf of separate products to piece together. Founded by Hossam El Maraghy, the business had been running for about four years by the time it reached Shark Tank Egypt, and it had built a base of roughly 20,000 customers. It sells and engages with customers through its Instagram and Facebook pages.

## Akoub (عكوب)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/akoub/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/akoub/
Sector: Agriculture
Outcome: no deal
Akoub pitched in Season 1, episode 2. The founders asked for 2.5M EGP for 15%, valuing the company at 16.7M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق عكوب مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٢. طلب المؤسسون ٢٫٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٥٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٦٫٧ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
Akoub AgriTech Services is an Egyptian agritech startup that uses agricultural drones, artificial intelligence and data analysis to pollinate date palms and spray pesticides. A drone can pollinate about 160 palms a day, compared with roughly 40 by hand, and the company targets Egypt's approximately 15 million palm trees. Its work also covers detecting palm diseases such as the red palm weevil and selling dates. Akoub was among the entries in the startup track of Ain Shams University's Innovate 2023 competition.

## Serket (سيركت)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/serket/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/serket/
Sector: Health
Founders: Shaimaa Mohamed
Outcome: deal
Serket pitched in Season 1, episode 2. The founders asked for 1M EGP for 30%, valuing the company at 3.3M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Abdallah Sallam: 1M EGP for 30%.
عرض فريق سيركت مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ٢. طلب المؤسسون ١ مليون ج.م مقابل ٣٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ٣٫٣ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع عبد الله سلام بقيمة ١ مليون ج.م مقابل ٣٠٪؜.
Serket is a scorpion farm in Qena, Upper Egypt, named after the ancient Egyptian scorpion goddess. Qena's intense heat makes it ideal scorpion habitat, so the creatures often spread into the streets and sting many residents. Founder Shaimaa, an agricultural engineer, set out to turn that local hazard into a resource: Serket breeds scorpions and extracts their venom for use in medicines and cosmetics, supplying pharmaceutical and cosmetics makers with a high-value raw material.
Sources: https://www.youm7.com/6048986 https://www.elwatannews.com/news/details/6405240 https://followict.news/%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%AA%D9%87%D8%A7%D8%A1-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D9%88%D8%B3%D9%85-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%88%D9%84-%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B4%D8%B1%D9%83%D8%A7%D8%AA/ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CQWWwLINWi0 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qeUKiwMzYws https://cairo360.com/?p=1725815 https://www.dostor.org/4283148

## Country's (كانتريز)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/countrys/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/countrys/
Sector: Food
Founders: Hind El Yamany
Outcome: deal
Country's pitched in Season 1, episode 1. The founders asked for 500K EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 5M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas and Ahmed El Sewedy: 700K EGP for 50%.
عرض فريق كانتريز مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١. طلب المؤسسون ٥٠٠ ألف ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ٥ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أيمن عباس وأحمد السويدي بقيمة ٧٠٠ ألف ج.م مقابل ٥٠٪؜.
Country's is an Egyptian healthy food brand built around one simple idea: real food should not depend on processed sugar. Founded by Hind El Yamany, it makes organic products sweetened with honey instead of refined sugar, giving health-conscious families a more natural option. The brand pitched in the very first episode of Shark Tank Egypt and left with backing from two sharks, Ayman Abbas and Ahmed El Sewedy.

## Habu Arts (هابو آرتس)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/habu-arts/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/habu-arts/
Sector: Home
Founders: Alaa Abdel Moghny
Outcome: no deal
Habu Arts pitched in Season 1, episode 1. The founders asked for 5M EGP for 7%, valuing the company at 71.4M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق هابو آرتس مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١. طلب المؤسسون ٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٧٪؜، أي بتقييم ٧١٫٤ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
Habu Arts is a Luxor-based workshop that makes handmade home accessories and decor from white alabaster, known locally as marmar. Its pieces blend ancient Egyptian art with modern design, aiming to revive a traditional craft that supports artisans on Luxor's west bank, and they are sold at the Grand Egyptian Museum. Founder Alaa Abdel Moghny asked the sharks for EGP 5 million for 7% but left without a deal.

## StepInside (ستيب إنسايد)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/stepinside/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/stepinside/
Sector: Tech
Founders: Hossam Sami
Outcome: no deal
StepInside pitched in Season 1, episode 1. The founders asked for 3M EGP for 20%, valuing the company at 15M EGP. They left without a deal.
عرض فريق ستيب إنسايد مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١. طلب المؤسسون ٣ مليون ج.م مقابل ٢٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ١٥ مليون ج.م. غادر الفريق دون صفقة.
StepInside is an Egyptian virtual-commerce (v-commerce) startup that builds immersive virtual stores for brands, so shoppers can walk through a shop online instead of scrolling a flat product grid. Billing itself as the first v-commerce platform in the MENA region, it uses virtual and augmented reality and 3D product viewers to help brands stand out online and sell more. Founded in 2021 and led by co-founder and CEO Hossam Sami, it has grown to a team of roughly 11 to 50 people.

## Dajin (داجن)
URL: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/en/dajin/ | Arabic: https://sharktank.ahmed-ibrahim.com/ar/dajin/
Sector: Agriculture
Founders: Mohamed Hesham
Outcome: deal
Dajin pitched in Season 1, episode 1. The founders asked for 5M EGP for 10%, valuing the company at 50M EGP. They walked away with a deal with Ayman Abbas and Mohamed Farouk: 5M EGP for 50%.
عرض فريق داجن مشروعه في الموسم ١، الحلقة ١. طلب المؤسسون ٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ١٠٪؜، أي بتقييم ٥٠ مليون ج.م. انتهى العرض بصفقة مع أيمن عباس ومحمد فاروق بقيمة ٥ مليون ج.م مقابل ٥٠٪؜.
Dajin is an agritech platform and app that helps small poultry farmers get feed and veterinary medicine and connects them with suppliers, buyers, markets and factories. Beyond its marketplaces it runs an academy for breeders and uses AI-based credit scoring to offer them financing. Founded in late 2022 and incubated by AUC Venture Lab and TIEC, it later joined the Ibtikar agritech accelerator. Founder Mohamed Hesham asked for EGP 5 million for 10%; Ayman Abbas pushed for half the company, and the final deal with Ayman Abbas and Mohamed Farouk was EGP 5 million for 50%.
